# Raj Kawale

> Product Lead at Indegene, building GenAI and Agentic AI products for healthcare. He helps healthcare organizations adopt AI in ways that fit real workflows, regulatory constraints, and business goals. He runs product like a founder: he owns the problem, the build, and the outcome. Outside work hours he is building KOS, an exocortex.

Raj Kawale is based in Bengaluru, India. Canonical profile: https://www.rajkawale.com/about

## Who he is

Product Lead, GenAI & Agentic AI at Indegene (May 2026–present). He takes a product from the first question to what actually ships, in a domain where "mostly right" isn't good enough.

That ownership comes from having been the founder. Across 6+ years in enterprise SaaS, AI, healthcare, and e-commerce, he has also built two products from scratch:

- RaiTalk — talk to your AI psychologist. A GenAI conversational platform. Idea to production in 2 weeks, 20% returning users without paid acquisition. Sunset when what he learned outgrew the product. https://www.rajkawale.com/work/raitalk
- Madhav Farm — a farm-to-consumer marketplace. ₹8L in GMV with zero working capital and an 8-person team. https://www.rajkawale.com/work/madhav-farm

Outside work hours he is building KOS, an exocortex: an AI that has to commit to a position and a probability before it answers, then gets scored against what actually happened. https://www.rajkawale.com/work/kos

## How he works

- Question before you build. The problem in the brief is rarely the real one.
- Learn from the root, not the trend. What lasts is why something works: user behaviour, the business model, and the constraints.
- Ship to learn. A shipped version teaches what a perfect plan never will.
- Commit, then get scored. Take a position, put a number on it, let reality grade you.
- Constraints beat resources. Madhav Farm did ₹8L in GMV on zero working capital.

## Who should talk to him

Founders, tech and product leaders, and investors thinking about where AI goes next. He wants to compare notes.
